newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler to merger Mercedes into parent - sources.
newsitem.headline: Daimler to merger Mercedes into parent - sources.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG will this month finalise long-awaited plans to merge its luxury automaker Mercedes-Benz into the parent company, sources close to the industrial giant said.
The sources said on Saturday that Daimler's supervisory board was expected to approve a proposal for a merger at its meeting scheduled for Jan. 23.
Daimler itself declined direct comment, merely repeating that the meeting this month would reach a final decision on Daimler's organisation.

There has been much speculation about the possible repercussions from Daimler's long-planned restructuring, which comes as chief executive Juergen Schrempp struggles to streamline the sprawling company, one of the largest in Germany.

The German media has reported repeatedly that Mercedes' highly respected chief executive Helmut Werner threatened to leave the Daimler group because of his opposition to Schrempp's plans and might do so if the merger went ahead.
The sources did not comment on Werner but said the new management board of the restructured Daimler group would not include a post carrying responsibility for the entire Mercedes group.
The sources were confirming a report this weekend in the Spiegel magazine, which said a decision had finally been reached on the future status of Mercedes in the Daimler group.

Spiegel had said that Hilmar Kopper, the outgoing Deutsche Bank AG chief executive who heads Daimler's supervisory board, and Karl Feuerstein, head of Daimler's works council, had indicated they approved the move.

The magazine also said that Mercedes future representation on the Daimler-Benz management board would comprise representatives of its car division, its commercial division and its distribution department.
Helmut Werner's fate was not yet clear, Spiegel said.
Werner reportedly opposes a merger of Mercedes into Daimler because of his fears that the automaker would be stripped of much of its independence by such a move.
Since Juergen Schrempp took the helm of Daimler in May 1995, the company has given up 11 of the 35 business divisions it once controlled.
